## Story-level uncertainties

- Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this provision and on the stone. None is used in this draft.
- The renderings 'manna', 'quails' and 'cloud' follow common usage; a scholar should confirm the wording for mann, salwa and ghamam.
- The first passage addresses 'you' and does not name the people of Musa; it is read together with the other passage, which does.
- Both passages state the number of the springs and the other passage states the number of the tribes; this draft does not write the number out because the shared number-word check has no anchor for it (its test keeps that word refused). A scholar should decide how the page states it.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Shade, food and water  (`#shade-food-and-water`)

Cited ayat: 2:57, 2:60, 7:160

> **2:57** وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

> **2:60** وَإِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ مِن رِّزْقِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

> **7:160** وَقَطَّعْنَٰهُمُ ٱثْنَتَىْ عَشْرَةَ أَسْبَاطًا أُمَمًا وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱسْتَسْقَىٰهُ قَوْمُهُۥٓ أَنِ ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ ٱلْحَجَرَ فَٱنۢبَجَسَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْغَمَٰمَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلْوَىٰ كُلُوا۟ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقْنَٰكُمْ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:57, 7:160): God shaded a people with the cloud and sent down on them manna and quails; 7:160 says this of the people of Musa.

**c2** (2:57, 7:160): They were told to eat of the good things God had provided; the ayat say that they did no wrong to God, but were wronging themselves.

**c3** (2:60, 7:160): In one passage Musa asks for water for his people, and in the other his people ask him for water.

**c4** (2:60, 7:160): God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it; the ayat state how many.

**c5** (2:60, 7:160): Every group of people knew its own drinking place.

**c6** (2:60): They were told to eat and drink of God's provision and not to spread corruption in the land.

**c7** (7:160): God divided them into tribes, as communities; the ayah states how many.

### One-minute summary

God shaded the people of Musa with the cloud and sent down manna and quails for them [c1]. When water was asked for, God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it [c3][c4].

### Complete story

The ayat remind a people that God shaded them with the cloud and sent down on them manna and quails [c1]. They were told to eat of the good things that God had provided for them [c2].

Both passages tell of a request for water: in one passage Musa asks for it for his people, and in the other his people ask him for it [c3]. God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out of it [c4]. Every group of people knew its own drinking place [c5].

They were told to eat and drink of God's provision and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. The other passage adds that God divided them into tribes, as communities [c7].

### Deep study

The passages use different verbs for the water coming out of the stone, and each states the number of the springs [c4]. Both passages end with the same statement: those who were given this provision did no wrong to God, but were wronging themselves [c2]. The division into tribes is stated in 7:160 only [c7].

### Kids mode

God shaded Musa's people with the cloud and sent them manna and quails to eat [c1]. When they needed water, God told Musa to strike the stone with his staff, and springs came out [c3][c4]. Each group knew where to drink [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that provision comes with an instruction, to eat of what is good and not to spread corruption in the land [c6]. Another is that the passages say wrongdoing harms the wrongdoers themselves and not God [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: what the cloud, the manna and the quails were like; the verses do not describe them, and the words used here are the common renderings.
- Not established: where this happened, when, or for how long the provision lasted.
- Not established: how the passages are ordered in time; the stone is not identified, and the verses do not say whether the water ran for a time or once.
- Not established: who exactly is addressed in the first passage; the other passage ties the same events to the people of Musa.
